emergency.heading: Barbados police emergency number:
emergency.detail: Barbados has three emergency numbers, not one. Dial 211 for the police, 511 for an ambulance and 311 for the fire service. English is the official language.
notices: Police 211, ambulance 511, fire 311. Barbados uses three separate emergency numbers, so save all three in your phone before you land.
The Queen Elizabeth Hospital on Martindale's Road, St Michael, is the main public hospital. Its switchboard is +1 246 436 6450.

faqs.question: What are the emergency numbers in Barbados?
faqs.answer: Barbados uses three numbers: 211 for the police, 511 for an ambulance and 311 for the fire service. They are listed by the Government of Barbados and by the UK Foreign Office travel advice for Barbados, checked in November 2026. Save all three before you travel, because each service has its own line.

faqs.question: How do I call an ambulance in Barbados?
faqs.answer: Dial 511 and ask for an ambulance, as the UK Foreign Office advises. The Queen Elizabeth Hospital lists its Accident and Emergency department as 246-436-6450 extension 5540, or 511. Tell the operator your parish, the nearest landmark and what has happened.

faqs.question: Who do I call in Barbados after a theft, a robbery or another crime?
faqs.answer: For an emergency or a crime in progress, dial 211. The Government of Barbados emergency shelter booklet also lists 430-7100 for the Police Department. For a theft that is not urgent, report it at a police station and keep the report reference for your insurer. The UK Foreign Office reports incidents of violent crime, including armed robbery, so keep valuables out of sight.

faqs.question: Which hospital do visitors use in Barbados?
faqs.answer: The Queen Elizabeth Hospital on Martindale's Road, St Michael, is the main public hospital; its switchboard is 246-436-6450. As of November 2026, its Accident and Emergency department provides care 24 hours a day, seven days a week. The UK Foreign Office says it can cope with many types of treatment, but serious cases may need emergency evacuation, and that medical treatment in Barbados can be expensive. Travel insurance that covers medical evacuation matters here.

faqs.question: I lost my passport in Barbados: who do I contact?
faqs.answer: Report the loss to the police, then contact your mission. British nationals: the British High Commission Consular Section is on +1 246 430 7800, and gov.uk says the office is temporarily closed to visitors after flooding, with emergency help through its online contact form. US citizens: the US Embassy at Wildey Business Park, St Michael, on 246-227-4000, the same number out of hours. Canadians: the High Commission of Canada on 1-246-629-3550, or the Emergency Watch and Response Centre in Ottawa on 1-888-949-9993.

faqs.question: Who do I call for an emergency at sea or on the beach?
faqs.answer: Dial 211 for the police or 511 for an ambulance. The Government of Barbados lists the Barbados Coast Guard at HMBS Pelican on 246-536-2900, with its Operations Room on 246-536-2947. The UK Foreign Office warns that currents can be deceptively strong, including on popular south and west coast beaches, that some beaches have no lifeguards or warning flags, and that swimming is not recommended on many east coast beaches.

faqs.question: What should I do if a hurricane or tropical storm threatens Barbados?
faqs.answer: The UK Foreign Office says the hurricane season normally runs from June to November. Follow local news and the instructions of the Department of Emergency Management, whose shelter booklet lists 438-7575, and your accommodation. In any emergency during a storm, use 211, 511 or 311 as usual.

faqs.question: What is the fire service number in Barbados?
faqs.answer: Dial 311 for the Barbados Fire Service. The Government of Barbados emergency shelter booklet also lists 535-7824 for the Fire Service. The numbers 311 (fire) and 511 (ambulance) are easy to mix up, so store them in your phone under clear names.

essentials.advisory: The UK Foreign Office page for Barbados was last updated on 23 January 2026 and was marked still current when we checked in November 2026. It reports incidents of violent crime, including armed robbery, sexual assault and carjacking, and an increase in gang-related murders involving guns. It also warns that currents can be deceptively strong, including on some popular south and west coast beaches, and that the hurricane season normally runs from June to November. The U.S. State Department advisory, issued 10 April 2026 and checked in November 2026, is Level 1: Exercise normal precautions.

tips.label: Tap water
tips.text: Watch for water notices: the Barbados Water Authority says a "Boil Water" notice is issued with the Ministry of Health if the supply becomes unsafe, for example after a storm, so ask your accommodation about the local supply and follow any notice in force

tips.label: Sun
tips.text: Use sunscreen and stay hydrated: cover up, reapply after swimming, drink water through the day and find shade around midday, especially on beaches with little natural cover

tips.label: Mosquitoes
tips.text: Avoid mosquito bites: the UK Foreign Office lists dengue, Zika and chikungunya among the health risks in Barbados, so use repellent and cover up throughout the day as well as at dawn and dusk

tips.label: At the beach
tips.text: The UK Foreign Office warns that currents can be deceptively strong, including on some popular south and west coast beaches, and that swimming is not recommended on many east coast beaches, where currents are particularly strong. Some beaches have no lifeguards or warning flags, and lifeguard stations are not staffed around the clock, so check conditions first and swim where a lifeguard is on duty.

tips.label: On the road
tips.text: Taxis in Barbados have no meters, so agree the fare before you get in; the Government of Barbados says fares are set by the government, and the Foreign Office notes that drivers do not always take cards, so carry cash. Barbados drives on the left. Visitors no longer buy a driving permit: the Barbados Revenue Authority says a Car Rental Levy replaced the Visitor Driving Permit on 15 October 2025, BBD 5 a day up to BBD 35 per rental as of November 2026, so bring your valid home licence.

guides.title: Barbados Currency and Money: Dollars, Cards and Tax
guides.summary: The Barbados dollar is fixed at BBD 2 to USD 1. US dollars and major cards are widely accepted, buses need exact local cash, and standard VAT is 17.5%.
guides.html:
Money in Barbados centres on the Barbados dollar, and the local currency has been fixed to the US dollar for half a century. Prices are shown in Barbados dollars (BBD, often written BDS$ or Bds$), US dollars are taken widely, and cards work in most hotels, shops and restaurants. The details that catch visitors out are smaller: the government bus requires the exact cash fare, taxis may want cash, and the tax on a bill depends on what you are buying.

This guide uses the Central Bank of Barbados, the Barbados Revenue Authority (BRA), the Barbados Transport Board, Visit Barbados and the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), as read in November 2026. Where we could not confirm a specific rule, we say so.

The short version

TopicWhat to know (as of November 2026)
CurrencyBarbados dollar (BBD)
Rate with the US dollarFixed at USD 1.00 to BBD 2.00 since July 1975 (Central Bank)
US dollars"Accepted island-wide" (Visit Barbados)
CardsMost stores and restaurants accept major credit cards (Visit Barbados); taxis do not always (FCDO)
Government busBDS$3.50 per trip, exact fare, no change given
VAT17.5% standard; 7.5% on accommodating direct tourism services; 22% on telecoms
Car rental levyBBD 5 per day, capped at BBD 35 per rental

The Barbados dollar: notes and coins

The Central Bank of Barbados first issued the national currency in 1973. According to the Bank, banknotes come in six denominations: $2, $5, $10, $20, $50 and $100, and circulation coins in four: 5 cents, 10 cents, 25 cents and 1 dollar. The one-cent coin stopped being issued in 2014. All notes are the same size, so check the colour and number rather than reaching for the biggest one.

Small coins matter more than you might expect. The government bus takes exact fares only, and roadside snacks, a coconut water on the beach at Accra Beach or a fish cake from a stall are easiest with small local change.

The 2 to 1 peg with the US dollar

The Central Bank describes how, on 5 July 1975, the Barbados dollar was fixed to the US dollar "at a rate of USD1.00 to BBD2.00", and that rate still holds. In practice this means one US dollar is worth two Barbados dollars, so a BDS$40 dinner is US$20. The Bank also publishes buying and selling rates for the public each business day, which is why the figure on a bank's exchange board is close to, but not exactly, 2.

Visit Barbados, the official tourism site, gives the rate on its travel information page as US$1 = BDS$1.98. This tourism-page figure differs from the Central Bank's official 2 to 1 peg. Ask your bank for its current buying rate. When a shop takes US dollars, ask what rate it applies before you pay.

For UK visitors, there is no fixed rate with the pound. The sterling value of a Barbados dollar moves with the pound against the US dollar, so check the rate shortly before you travel.

Paying in US dollars

Visit Barbados says "US dollars are accepted island-wide". That makes US cash a reasonable backup for American and Canadian visitors in particular. Two practical points follow. First, you may receive change in Barbados dollars, so it helps to pay with smaller US notes. Second, the Transport Board states its fare in Barbados dollars and requires the exact amount in the farebox, so carry the exact local cash fare for it.

Pounds sterling and other currencies

We found no official statement that shops or restaurants accept pounds sterling, euros or Canadian dollars in cash, so do not plan on spending them directly. British visitors are better served by a card for larger purchases and Barbados dollars (from an ATM or a bank) for small ones. Our first-timer's guide has more on what to pack and plan.

Cards: where they work and where they do not

According to Visit Barbados, most stores and restaurants accept major credit cards, which covers most spending in resort areas such as Holetown and Hastings and Worthing; confirm with your hotel when you book. The FCDO's advice for taxis is the important exception: drivers do not always accept card payments, so carry cash. The same caution makes sense for small beach vendors, rum shops and food stalls.

When a card terminal or ATM offers to charge you in your home currency instead of Barbados dollars, choosing the local currency usually leaves the exchange rate with your own card issuer rather than the terminal operator. Check your bank's foreign transaction fees before you go.

ATMs and exchanging money

Bank branches are concentrated in Bridgetown and the larger coastal towns; if you want cash on landing at Grantley Adams International Airport, check the airport's own information before you fly. Visit Barbados says ATMs only dispense local currency, so expect Barbados dollars from a cash machine. Your own bank may charge a foreign withdrawal fee on top of any fee the local machine shows on screen.

To change cash, use a bank or an exchange counter and compare the rate with the 2 to 1 peg: a US dollar rate close to 2 is fair, and anything well below it is costly. For pounds or euros, compare the offered rate with the current market rate.

The FCDO's safety advice applies here too: take care when taking money from ATMs, and do not carry large amounts of cash. Our Barbados safety guide sets out the full advisory.

VAT and other charges on your bill

The Barbados Revenue Authority lists four VAT rates, as of November 2026:

  • 17.5%, the rate for standard supplies, which covers most purchases;
  • 7.5%, on accommodating direct tourism services;
  • 22%, on telecommunications services (relevant if you buy a local SIM or data);
  • 0%, on zero-rated items.

Check whether a menu or quote already includes VAT before you pay. The BRA's own example of a car rental quote shows how the pieces are itemised: a base price of $100.00, a Car Rental Levy of $5.00 (not subject to VAT), VAT at 17.5% on the base price of $17.50, and a total of $122.50.

That levy is new. Since 15 October 2025 the BRA charges a Car Rental Levy of BBD 5.00 per day on every vehicle rental, capped at BBD 35.00 per rental (seven days), and it applies per rental, not per driver. On the same date the Visitor Driving Permit was abolished: visitors must show a valid driving licence to the rental company and check any other rental requirements. Our getting around Barbados guide covers renting and driving on the left.

Service charge and tipping

As of November 2026, Visit Barbados says gratuities of 10 to 15 percent are automatically added to bills in many places. This describes a practice, rather than a compulsory extra tip. Read the bill before you add anything: if a service charge line is already there, an extra tip is your choice, not an obligation. If no service charge appears and you were well looked after, leaving something for the staff is appreciated, in cash where possible so it reaches the person who served you.

For taxis, the FCDO says taxis do not have meters, that there are standard fares for most destinations, and that you should agree the fare in Barbados dollars before you set off. Agreeing the fare first is the simplest way to avoid a dispute over change or tips at the end of the ride.

What things cost, in words

The only prices we quote are the ones set by official bodies. The Transport Board's fare is BDS$3.50 per trip, as of November 2026, with the exact fare required and no change or refund given, and the Board says it is rolling out a cashless fare system in phases. That makes the bus a low-cost option for journeys from Oistins to Speightstown.

Beyond that, expect a wide range. Eating at a fish fry such as the Oistins Fish Fry or from a local lunch spot costs far less than a sit-down restaurant on the west coast. A rum punch at a rum shop and the same drink at a beach-club bar can cost different amounts. Paid attractions such as Harrison's Cave, St Nicholas Abbey and boat trips like catamaran cruises set their own prices, so check the operator's site before you budget. Imported goods in supermarkets carry the cost of shipping to an island. Free pleasures are plentiful: most beaches, from Carlisle Bay to Mullins, cost nothing to visit.

Peak periods push accommodation prices up. Our best time to visit Barbados and Barbados in winter guides explain when demand is highest, and the 5-day itinerary shows a balanced mix of free and paid days.

A practical money checklist

  • Tell your bank you are travelling and check its foreign transaction and ATM fees.
  • Carry two cards from different networks in case one is declined.
  • Get some Barbados dollars on arrival, including coins for the bus.
  • US visitors: bring some small US notes as a backup.
  • Agree every taxi fare in Barbados dollars before setting off.
  • Check bills for VAT and any service charge before adding a tip.
  • Keep valuables and spare cash in a hotel safe, as the FCDO advises.

Before you land, complete the Barbados immigration and customs form, and save the emergency contacts page. More practical notes are on our local tips page.

Frequently Asked Questions

What currency is used in Barbados?

The Barbados dollar (BBD). The Central Bank issues notes of $2, $5, $10, $20, $50 and $100, and coins of 5, 10 and 25 cents and 1 dollar. Prices are normally shown in Barbados dollars, so check which currency a price is in before you pay.

Is the Barbados dollar fixed to the US dollar?

Yes. The Central Bank of Barbados fixed the rate at USD 1.00 to BBD 2.00 on 5 July 1975, and that peg still holds. Banks quote buying and selling rates close to that figure, so the rate you get when exchanging cash can be a little under 2.

Can I use US dollars in Barbados?

Generally yes: Visit Barbados says US dollars are accepted island-wide. Expect change in Barbados dollars. For the government bus, carry the exact local cash fare: BDS$3.50 as of November 2026.

Can I pay with pounds sterling in Barbados?

We found no official source saying shops accept pounds in cash, so do not count on it. Use a card for larger payments and withdraw or exchange Barbados dollars for small purchases, taxis and buses.

Are credit cards accepted in Barbados?

Visit Barbados says most stores and restaurants accept major credit cards. The FCDO notes that taxi drivers do not always accept cards, so carry cash for taxis, small vendors and the bus.

What is the VAT rate in Barbados?

The Barbados Revenue Authority lists 17.5% for standard supplies, 7.5% on accommodating direct tourism services, 22% on telecommunications services and 0% on zero-rated items, as of November 2026.

Do you tip in Barbados?

As of November 2026, Visit Barbados says gratuities of 10 to 15 percent are added in many places. Check the bill first: if a service charge is already included, any extra is optional. If it is not, a cash tip for good service is appreciated. For taxis, agree the fare in Barbados dollars before setting off, as the FCDO advises.

guides.title: Barbados for First-Timers: Coasts, Money, Rules
guides.summary: Everything for a first visit to Barbados: west, south or east coast, how many days, the free online immigration and customs form, the 2 to 1 dollar peg, BDS$3.50 buses, taxis without meters, driving on the left and the camouflage ban.
guides.html:
Barbados is one of the easier Caribbean islands for a first visit: English is the language, the roads and buses reach most of the island, and the US dollar is accepted almost everywhere. A few things still catch first-timers out, from the online entry form to the rule on camouflage clothing. This guide covers the decisions to make before you book and the practical details for the first day on the ground.

How the island is laid out

Barbados is compact, but the coasts feel very different.

  • West coast (St James and St Peter): calm Caribbean water, the area around Holetown and Speightstown, with many of the island's upscale hotels and villas.
  • Bridgetown (St Michael): the capital, the cruise port and the UNESCO-listed Historic Bridgetown and its Garrison.
  • South coast (Christ Church): a lively strip, from Hastings and Worthing to St Lawrence Gap and Oistins, close to the airport.
  • South east (St Philip): cliffs and coves around the Crane.
  • East coast (St Joseph and St Andrew): Atlantic surf and the green hills of the Scotland District around Bathsheba.
  • North: cliffs and quiet country in St Lucy.

All international flights land at Grantley Adams International Airport (BGI) in Christ Church, on the south side of the island.

Which coast to choose

Most first-timers stay on the west or the south coast. Choose the west for calm swimming, snorkelling and sunsets, and the south for more restaurants, nightlife, a wider spread of prices and a short airport transfer. The east coast is beautiful but the sea there is mostly not for swimming, so it is better as a day trip or a quiet extra night. Our guide to where to stay in Barbados compares each area in detail.

How many days

Three days covers a beach, Bridgetown and one inland sight; follow our 3-day itinerary. Five days lets you add a turtle trip and the east coast (5-day itinerary). Consider a week, with time for rum, caves, gardens and a Friday at the fish fry; see the 7-day itinerary or, with children, the family version. For timing, read the best time to visit Barbados; the hurricane season normally runs from June to November.

The entry form

Every traveller must complete the online Immigration and Customs Form before arriving. The official site is travelform.gov.bb. According to Visit Barbados, the form becomes available 72 hours before your arrival, and the Immigration and Customs receipts are emailed to you, to be saved on your phone or printed and shown to officers on arrival. You need a valid email address, your passport and your flight details.

The form is free. WINAIR lists the Barbados ED form as free as of November 2026. CARICOM IMPACS has warned about fraudulent immigration-form websites targeting Barbados travellers. If a website asks for payment, close it. Our step-by-step guide to the immigration and customs form walks through each screen.

Visa rules depend on your passport. British visitors, for example, do not need a visa and are told on arrival how long they can stay, and their passport must be valid for the planned length of the stay. The Immigration Department page returned conflicting passport-validity wording during our check, including a six-month requirement. Confirm with Immigration and your airline. Check the rules for your nationality on our visa requirements page before you book.

Money and the dollar peg

The local currency is the Barbados dollar (BBD, written Bds$ or BDS$). It is fixed to the US dollar at two Barbados dollars to one US dollar, a peg the Central Bank of Barbados has held for decades. In practice, Visit Barbados notes that the US dollar typically exchanges at about Bds$1.98, slightly under the peg, while the official peg remains 2 to 1.

Major credit cards and US dollars are accepted island-wide, but ATMs dispense local currency only. Check whether a price is in BBD or USD before you pay, since a menu price of 40 means something very different in each. Carry small Barbados dollar notes and coins for buses, beach snacks and taxis. More detail is in our guide to Barbados currency and money.

Buses and taxis

The government-owned Barbados Transport Board runs buses across the island, with main terminals in Bridgetown. As of November 2026 the fare is BDS$3.50 per trip, and you must put the exact fare in the farebox: no change is given. The Board is rolling out a cashless fare system in phases. Privately owned yellow minibuses with a blue stripe run selected routes for the same BDS$3.50, and white ZR vans with a maroon stripe cover their own numbered routes. Buses along the south and west coast roads are the easiest for visitors to use.

Taxis do not use meters. Fares are regulated by the government and there are standard fares for most destinations, but agree the price before you get in, and carry cash, since drivers do not always take cards. Many drivers also offer island tours at a flat rate. Our guide to getting around Barbados and the transportation page cover routes and airport transfers.

Driving on the left and the old visitor permit

Traffic drives on the left. Roads are narrow away from the main highways, signage can be thin in the countryside, and the roundabouts near Bridgetown get busy at rush hour.

A change many older guides miss: the Visitor Driving Permit was abolished when the Car Rental Levy took effect on 15 October 2025. As of November 2026, the Barbados Revenue Authority describes the levy as BBD $5.00 per day, up to a maximum of $35.00 per rental, collected by the rental company when you hire the car. You still need a valid driving licence; the Canadian government advises carrying an International Driving Permit if your licence is not in English. Ask your rental company what it requires.

Plugs and power

Visit Barbados gives the supply as 115/230 volts at 50 cycles, with plugs of two flat blades, some with a round grounding pin (Type A and B). Check your device's voltage and frequency rating and plug type, and ask your accommodation which adaptor or converter you may need. Ask your accommodation if one is provided in the room.

Tap water

Tap water is safe to drink. Visit Barbados describes the island's water as perfectly safe to drink from the tap, so a refillable bottle saves money and plastic.

Tipping

Look at the bill first. As of November 2026, Visit Barbados notes that gratuities of 10 to 15 percent are automatically added to the bill in many places. Where a service charge is included, extra tipping is optional. Where it is not, an additional tip is your choice. Ask your hotel which room charges apply.

The camouflage law

It is illegal for anyone in Barbados, including children, to wear camouflage clothing. The Canadian government adds that carrying items made of camouflage material is also an offence for civilians. Leave camouflage shorts, swimwear, caps and bags at home.

Safety basics

Barbados is a popular, well-visited island, but the UK government reports incidents of violent crime, including armed robbery, and an increase in gang-related murders involving guns, some in populated public areas. Take normal precautions: do not carry large amounts of cash or wear expensive-looking jewellery. In an emergency, dial 211 for police, 511 for an ambulance and 311 for the fire service. Read more in is Barbados safe and on our emergency contacts page.

Common first-timer mistakes

  • Paying for the entry form on a lookalike site. The official form is free.
  • Swimming on the east coast. The UK government advises that swimming is not recommended on many east-coast beaches because of strong currents. Strong currents can also affect south- and west-coast beaches. Follow local warnings and take care wherever you swim.
  • Packing camouflage. It is against the law to wear it.
  • Getting on the bus without the exact fare. No change is given.
  • Not agreeing a taxi fare first. There are no meters.
  • Confusing BBD and USD prices. Ask which currency a price is in.
  • Doubling the tip. Check the bill for a service charge.
  • Trying to see everything from one base in three days. Pick a coast and add one or two day trips. Our list of things to do in Barbados helps you choose, and local tips has more.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need to fill in a form before flying to Barbados?

Yes. All travellers must complete the online Immigration and Customs Form at travelform.gov.bb before arriving. It opens 72 hours before arrival, it is free, and you show the emailed receipts, on your phone or printed, to Immigration and Customs when you land.

Can I use US dollars in Barbados?

Yes. Major credit cards and US dollars are accepted island-wide, and the Barbados dollar is fixed at two to one US dollar. ATMs give local currency only, so expect change in Barbados dollars too.

Do I still need a visitor driving permit to drive in Barbados?

No. The Visitor Driving Permit was abolished when the Car Rental Levy took effect on 15 October 2025. As of November 2026 the rental company collects a levy of BBD $5.00 per day, up to $35.00 per rental. You still need a valid driving licence.

How much is the bus in Barbados?

As of November 2026, the Transport Board fare is BDS$3.50 per trip, paid with the exact amount because no change is given. Yellow minibuses charge the same fare.

Is it illegal to wear camouflage in Barbados?

Yes. It is illegal for anyone, including children, to wear camouflage clothing in Barbados. Leave any camouflage items at home.

Can you drink the tap water in Barbados?

Yes. Visit Barbados describes the tap water as perfectly safe to drink.

guides.title: Barbados Immigration and Customs Form: How to Fill It In
guides.summary: Complete the Barbados Immigration and Customs Form at travelform.gov.bb, which opens 72 hours before arrival. Save the emailed receipts and carry your return ticket and address.
guides.html:
Every arrival in Barbados now starts online. Before you fly, you fill in the Barbados Immigration and Customs Form (still often called the ED form) on the government portal, receive the receipts by email, and show them to the immigration and customs officers at Grantley Adams International Airport. This guide uses the Barbados Immigration Department, Visit Barbados and official travel advice checked in November 2026. The live portal could not be opened during this check.

The one official address is travelform.gov.bb. Type it into your browser yourself rather than clicking a search advert. The rest of your arrival paperwork, from passport validity to the address where you will stay, is covered further down and on our visa requirements page.

The form at a glance (as of November 2026)

QuestionWhat the official sources say
Official sitetravelform.gov.bb (the Barbados Online Customs and Immigration Portal)
Who must complete it"Travellers are required" to complete it (Immigration Department); "All travellers" (gov.uk)
When it opens72 hours before your arrival in Barbados
What you needHave travel details and passports ready; a valid email address is required
What you receiveImmigration and Customs receipts, emailed when you submit
What you show on arrivalThe receipts, saved on your phone or printed
CostFree according to WINAIR, as of November 2026; use the official portal

Who must complete it

The Immigration Department says travellers are required to complete the online Immigration and Customs Form. The UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) puts it more broadly on its Barbados entry page: all travellers must fill in the immigration and customs form online before they arrive. The airport operator, GAIA Inc., says all arriving visitors are required to submit a correctly completed immigration and customs form.

What none of the official pages we could open states in words is whether a family or group travelling together needs one form each or can share one. We could not open the live form or the government FAQ to verify the current rule for couples, families or groups. If you are travelling as a family, read the current form instructions and, if in doubt, check with the Barbados Immigration Department through its website, immigration.gov.bb.

When to fill it in

The form "will be available 72 hours prior to your arrival in Barbados", in the Immigration Department's words. That window is counted from your arrival in Barbados, not from your departure, so a traveller on an overnight connection should count back from the landing time. The Immigration Department adds: "Fill in the form at a time and place convenient for you." We could not verify a separate latest submission deadline, and the receipts are what you show on landing, so finish it before you leave home and before you lose reliable internet in transit.

Arriving by sea or in transit through another island? Check arrival paperwork with your carrier or the Immigration Department. Cruise passengers should follow their cruise line's instructions as well, since we did not find an official page dealing with cruise calls specifically.

Step by step on the official portal

  1. Open travelform.gov.bb. Visit Barbados and the Immigration Department direct travellers to this official address.
  2. Gather your travel information. Have your flight details and passports ready. Visit Barbados says a valid email address is required to receive the receipts.
  3. Start your submission. Follow the current instructions on the official portal. We could not verify its button labels during this check.
  4. Work through the questions. Use your travel documents and answer the questions shown on the portal. The current section order could not be verified.
  5. Give a full local address. GAIA says arriving visitors must supply immigration with the full address of where they will be staying. Have the hotel, guest house or villa address to hand; our guide to where to stay in Barbados covers the main areas, from Holetown to St Lawrence Gap.
  6. Answer the customs questions honestly. The FCDO says there are strict rules about goods brought into and taken out of Barbados, and that you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.
  7. Submit and check your inbox. Visit Barbados, the official tourism site, says the Immigration and Customs receipts are emailed to travellers upon submission.
  8. Save or print the receipts. Visit Barbados says to save the receipts to your mobile device or print them and present them on arrival.

Is it free? Look-alike paid sites

As of November 2026, WINAIR lists the Barbados ED form as free. CARICOM IMPACS warns that fraudulent websites targeting Barbados travellers charge fees for fake forms. Use travelform.gov.bb and check the address before entering personal information.

The practical rule is simple. If a site asks for card details to "process" your Barbados immigration form, it is not travelform.gov.bb. Check the address bar before you type a passport number.

What you show on arrival

At immigration you present your passport and the Immigration receipt; at customs, the Customs receipt. Keep both reachable without wifi: save the receipts on your device or print them before travel, and a printout is a sensible backup. If you need to change something after submitting, check the current portal instructions or contact the Immigration Department. We could not verify its editing function.

Once you are through, our transport page and the getting around Barbados guide cover the trip from the airport in Christ Church to Bridgetown, Speightstown or the south coast.

If you have not done it

We could not find an official page we were able to open that sets out what happens to a traveller who lands without having completed the online form. Government information pages that may cover this (the Government Information Service) blocked our access when we checked in November 2026, so we are not repeating second-hand claims about kiosks or paper forms. The safe course is to complete the form before you fly. If the portal fails for you, contact the Barbados Immigration Department through immigration.gov.bb before departure, and ask your airline at check-in.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Using a look-alike site. Only travelform.gov.bb is official. Third-party sites can charge you and still leave you without a valid submission.
  • Trying too early. The form opens 72 hours before arrival. A week ahead is too soon.
  • A mistyped email address. The receipts are emailed. Check the address carefully so you can receive the receipts.
  • No local address. GAIA requires the full address where you will stay. "Touring the island" is not an address.
  • Forgetting the return journey. Immigration can ask for a return ticket (see below).
  • Packing camouflage. The FCDO says it is illegal for anyone, including children, to wear camouflage clothing in Barbados. Leave it at home.
  • Carrying a bag for someone else. The FCDO's advice is to pack your luggage yourself and not carry anything through customs for anyone else.

What else border officers may ask for

The form does not replace the usual entry checks. The Barbados Immigration Department's visitor page lists the following entry requirements, as read in November 2026:

  • a passport "valid for at least six (6) months";
  • a "Return ticket to country of residence";
  • your "Intended Address";
  • "Evidence of personal support" (the page names no amount of money).

The UK FCDO's wording differs slightly: it says your passport must be valid for the planned length of your stay and that visitors must be able to show an onward or return ticket. The Immigration page returned conflicting wording during our checks: the direct page and Firecrawl said six months, while the web tool returned validity for the trip. Check with Immigration and your airline before departure; six months remains the precaution used here. The FCDO also says British visitors do not need a visa, that you are told on arrival how long you can stay, and that extensions are applied and paid for through the Barbados Immigration Department.

The FCDO adds a health rule: if you arrive from a country listed as a yellow fever transmission risk, you must have a certificate proving vaccination. GAIA notes that travellers from select countries need Barbadian visas, so check your nationality on our visa requirements page.

Children: the Immigration Department says an unaccompanied minor under 18 must carry a written consent letter from a parent or legal guardian, signed by a notary public with the notary's seal, stating the duration of stay; a minor travelling with an adult who is not a parent or legal guardian needs a consent letter from a parent, also signed and sealed by a notary public. Include the duration of stay, the accompanying adult's identity, address and telephone number, and the receiving adult's details if different. For an unaccompanied minor, identify the authorised receiving adult and include their contact details; a legal guardian must carry proof of guardianship. Travel with the original and a copy. Families planning a holiday can start with our 7-day family itinerary.

US travellers: the US State Department's guidance, dated 22 October 2026 and read in November 2026, says you must show proof of future plans to leave Barbados. Check its current guidance and your carrier's document requirements before departure.

After arrival: the first day

With the paperwork done, the first decisions are money and transport. Our Barbados currency and money guide explains the 2 to 1 peg with the US dollar and paying for buses and taxis, and is Barbados safe sets out what the official travel advisories say. Save the emergency contacts page before you land.

First-time visitors should read the first-timer's guide and pick a pace from our 3-day or 7-day itinerary. A first evening at the Oistins Fish Fry or a swim at Carlisle Bay is easy from most south and west coast bases, and our best time to visit guide covers the seasons. If your trip falls in summer, check the Crop Over guide, as the festival brings busy flights.

What we could not confirm

  • Whether families or groups complete one form or one per person.
  • What happens on arrival if you have not completed the form.
  • The live portal's payment wording; WINAIR lists the Barbados ED form as free.
  • The current portal screens, editing function and latest submission deadline.

We will update this guide when an official source states these points. Our local tips page collects other practical notes.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the official website for the Barbados immigration form?

The official site is travelform.gov.bb, titled the Barbados Online Customs and Immigration Portal. Visit Barbados and the UK FCDO both point to that address. Type it in yourself: CARICOM IMPACS has warned about fraudulent immigration-form websites targeting Barbados travellers.

How far in advance can I complete the Barbados ED form?

The Immigration Department says the form is available 72 hours before your arrival in Barbados. Count back from your landing time, not your departure. We could not verify a separate latest deadline. Complete it before travel and keep the emailed receipts available on arrival.

Does the Barbados immigration and customs form cost anything?

WINAIR lists the Barbados ED form as free, as of November 2026. Use travelform.gov.bb, the official address identified by Barbados Immigration and Visit Barbados. Avoid paid look-alike sites.

Does every family member need a separate form?

We could not confirm this from an official page. We could not open the live portal or the government FAQ to verify the family rule. Follow the current official instructions and check with the Barbados Immigration Department if unsure.

What do I show at Barbados immigration?

Your passport and the Immigration and Customs receipts emailed to you when you submitted the form, saved on your phone or printed. The Immigration Department also lists a return ticket to your country of residence, your intended address and evidence of personal support as entry requirements.

How long must my passport be valid for Barbados?

The Barbados Immigration Department's visitor page says at least six months. The UK FCDO says valid for the planned length of your stay. The same Immigration URL returned conflicting wording during our checks. Confirm with Immigration and your airline; six months is a precaution, not a guarantee of admission.

Can I edit the form after submitting it?

We could not verify the current editing function. Check the official portal instructions or contact the Barbados Immigration Department if your flight or accommodation changes.

guides.title: Barbados in Winter: December to April Guide
guides.summary: December to April falls in the Barbados dry season: highs around 29C to 30C, high monthly sunshine averages, calm west coast water and a busy events calendar, so book early.
guides.html:
Why Barbados works in winter

From December to April, Barbados is in its dry season, which runs to May. Visit Barbados, the official tourism site, describes this part of the year, the northern hemisphere winter and spring, as the time when temperatures are a little cooler and there is less rain. For anyone leaving a British, American or Canadian winter, that means highs close to 30C, warm sea and long sunny days, a flight away.

It is also when everyone else has the same idea. Winter is peak season, so compare availability and prices before choosing your dates. This guide covers what the weather does, how the sea behaves on each coast, what is on, and how to plan around the crowds.

Winter weather: the official numbers

These figures come from the Barbados Meteorological Services (BMS) climate data sheet and are averages for 1991 to 2020. The sheet gives the service's address as Charnocks, Christ Church, but does not identify the observing station. Use the monthly figures for broad planning, rather than as a forecast for your arrival at Grantley Adams International Airport.

MonthAverage highAverage lowRainfallRain daysSunshine a day
December29.6C (85F)23.9C (75F)91.0mm118.2 hours
January29.1C (84F)23.3C (74F)68.1mm118.5 hours
February29.2C (85F)23.0C (73F)41.7mm98.8 hours
March29.7C (85F)23.4C (74F)38.9mm88.8 hours
April30.2C (86F)24.2C (76F)58.1mm88.7 hours

Three things stand out. First, rainfall falls towards March, then rises in April: December averages 91mm of rain, compared with 38.9mm in March and 58.1mm in April. Second, February and March share the highest monthly sunshine average in the 1991 to 2020 table, 8.8 hours a day. Third, nights are mild rather than cool, with average lows of 23C to 24C. The sheet lists a minimum temperature of 16.5C on 2 January 1984; this extreme does not describe a typical night.

The north-east trade winds, which Visit Barbados says blow almost every day, keep the heat comfortable and the air moving. December falls just after the official Atlantic hurricane season, which the US National Hurricane Center sets as 1 June to 30 November, so the whole December to April window sits outside it.

Sea conditions on each coast

Visit Barbados puts sea temperatures at 26C to 29C (79F to 84F) all year round, so the water is warm in winter too. What differs is the coast.

West coast

The coast from Holetown to Speightstown faces the Caribbean Sea, in the lee of the trade winds. It is the island's calm-water side and the classic winter-sun base. Paynes Bay, Mullins Beach and Folkestone Beach, next to Folkestone Marine Park, offer options for snorkelling. For turtle encounters, read our guide to swimming with turtles.

Carlisle Bay and the south coast

Carlisle Bay, just south of Bridgetown, sits within Carlisle Bay Marine Park and is a popular base for scuba diving. Further along the south coast, Accra Beach and Dover Beach sit close to the hotels and restaurants of the south coast, and towards the south-east tip, Silver Sands Beach is more exposed to the trade winds that drive kitesurfing and windsurfing.

East coast

The Atlantic coast around Bathsheba faces straight into the wind and swell. The UK Foreign Office travel advice for Barbados says swimming is not recommended on many east coast beaches, where currents are particularly strong. Go for the scenery, a walk along Cattlewash Beach and the surf at Bathsheba Beach, but swim on the west or south coast.

The same advice warns that currents can be deceptively strong even on some popular south and west coast beaches, that some beaches have no lifeguards or warning flags, and that lifeguard stations are not staffed around the clock. Swim near a lifeguard where you can, and ask locally before getting in.

What is on, December to April

December: Independence season, the marathon and Christmas

The season opens just after Independence Day on 30 November. Early December brings Run Barbados, which Visit Barbados lists from 4 to 6 December 2026, with a route through historic Bridgetown. Book ahead if travelling over Christmas or New Year.

January: Barbados Sailing Week

Barbados Sailing Week is listed by Visit Barbados for 15 to 21 January 2027, with racing off the island and social events ashore. Even if you are not sailing, a catamaran cruise along the west coast is a good way to see the fleet and the coastline.

February: the Holetown Festival

The Holetown Festival marks the arrival of the first settlers at Holetown on 17 February 1627. The festival's official site gives the 2027 dates as 14 to 21 February, which makes 17 February 2027 the 400th anniversary of that landing. Visit Barbados describes the week as folk singing and dancing, sports and games, street parades, markets and food stalls.

March: the Sandy Lane Gold Cup

The Sandy Lane Gold Cup is the big day of horse racing at the Garrison, run over 1,800 metres on turf at the Garrison Savannah, where Visit Barbados says racing has taken place since 1845. The 2026 race was held on 7 March. As of November 2026, the Barbados Turf Club lists Saturday 6 March 2027 for the Gold Cup, with racing dates subject to change. Recheck before booking around it. Away from the track, polo and golf are other ways to spend a dry winter afternoon.

April: Easter and the Oistins Fish Festival

Easter Sunday falls on 28 March in 2027, so the Easter weekend lands at the end of March rather than in April. The Oistins Fish Festival takes place every Easter weekend in Oistins, Christ Church. Good Friday and Easter Monday are public holidays, which affects opening hours; see our Barbados public holidays 2027 list.

Booking pressure and prices

Winter is peak season, and the pressure is not even across it. Compare flights and accommodation early if travelling over Christmas, New Year, UK February half-term or Easter.

A few ways to manage it:

  • Book flights and accommodation as early as you can for Christmas, February and Easter.
  • Compare early December, mid-January and late April with your holiday-week options.
  • Look beyond the west coast. The south coast around Hastings and Worthing and St Lawrence Gap offers places to stay.
  • Book popular excursions, restaurant tables and race-day tickets ahead in high season.

Our guide to where to stay in Barbados compares the main bases.

Winter is also the season when inland sightseeing is most comfortable, with the lowest average highs of the year. A day at Harrison's Cave, a walk at Hunte's Gardens or a drive north to St Nicholas Abbey makes a good break from the beach. For a ready-made plan, see the 7-day Barbados itinerary.

What to pack

  • Light cotton or linen clothes for days around 29C to 30C, and one light layer for evenings and air-conditioned rooms.
  • High-factor sunscreen, a hat and sunglasses: February and March average 8.8 hours of sunshine a day on the BMS record.
  • A compact umbrella or light rain jacket, mainly for December and January, which still average 11 rain days each.
  • Reef shoes and snorkel gear if you have your own.
  • Smart-casual clothes for evening dining and race days.
  • No camouflage: the UK Foreign Office advice notes that it is illegal for anyone in Barbados, children included, to wear camouflage clothing.
  • The right plug adapter: check the local tips page for plug types and voltage before you buy one.

Before you fly, read the entry requirements, the immigration and customs form guide and our first-timers guide.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Barbados warm in winter?

Yes. On the Barbados Meteorological Services 1991 to 2020 normals, average daily highs run from 29.1C (84F) in January to 30.2C (86F) in April, with average lows of 23C to 24C. Visit Barbados gives sea temperatures of 26C to 29C all year.

Does it rain in Barbados in winter?

Less than at any other time of year. March is the driest month, averaging 38.9mm over about 8 rain days, and February is close behind. December and January are a little wetter, averaging 91.0mm and 68.1mm, usually as short showers.

Is December to April outside hurricane season?

Yes. The US National Hurricane Center sets the official Atlantic hurricane season as 1 June to 30 November, so December to April falls outside it.

Can you swim on the east coast of Barbados in winter?

The UK Foreign Office advice says swimming is not recommended on many east coast beaches because currents are particularly strong. Swim on the calmer west coast or at Carlisle Bay, and visit Bathsheba for the views and the surf.

When is Barbados Sailing Week 2027?

Visit Barbados lists Barbados Sailing Week 2027 from 15 to 21 January 2027.

When is the Holetown Festival in 2027?

The festival's official site gives the 2027 dates as 14 to 21 February. It commemorates the arrival of the first settlers at Holetown on 17 February 1627.

What is the cheapest time to visit Barbados in winter?

Avoid the Christmas and New Year fortnight, the UK February half-term and Easter. Compare early December, mid-January and late April too; availability and prices depend on the property and flight.

guides.title: Barbados Public Holidays 2027: Dates and Closures
guides.summary: Barbados has 12 public holidays in 2027 under the Public Holidays Act; Emancipation Day moves to Tuesday 3 August and Boxing Day to Monday 27 December.
guides.html:
Barbados public holidays in 2027 at a glance

Barbados sets its public holidays in the Public Holidays Act (Cap. 352). The Act lists twelve days in its First Schedule, with fixed rules for when a date falls on a Sunday. As of November 2026, the Government of Barbados calendar lists the 2027 holidays and substitute days. The table below follows those dates and the Act, with Easter Sunday falling on 28 March 2027. Recheck the official calendar before travel, because additional holidays or substitutions can be appointed by order.

HolidayDate in 2027WeekdayNote
New Year's Day1 JanuaryFriday
Errol Barrow Day21 JanuaryThursday
Good Friday26 MarchFridayEaster Sunday is 28 March
Easter Monday29 MarchMonday
National Heroes Day28 AprilWednesday
Labour Day (May Day)1 MaySaturdayFalls on a Saturday; the Act moves only Sunday dates
Whit Monday17 MayMondayThe day after Pentecost
Kadooment Day2 AugustMondayThe first Monday in August
Emancipation Day (1 August falls on a Sunday)3 AugustTuesdayMoved under the Act's rule for 1 August
Independence Day30 NovemberTuesday
Christmas Day25 DecemberSaturday
Boxing Day (26 December falls on a Sunday)27 DecemberMondayMoved under the Act's Sunday rule

That is twelve holidays, observed on weekdays or Saturdays, with two of them (Emancipation Day and Boxing Day) shifted off a Sunday under the Act.

The rule for holidays that fall on a weekend

The First Schedule of the Act lists most fixed-date holidays with the words "if a week day", then sets out what happens when one falls on a Sunday:

  • If 1 January, 21 January, 28 April, 1 May, 30 November or 26 December falls on a Sunday, the next Monday is a public holiday.
  • If 1 August falls on a Sunday or a Monday, the next Tuesday is a public holiday. This is because the first Monday in August is already Kadooment Day.
  • If 25 December falls on a Sunday, the next Tuesday is a public holiday (the Monday is already Boxing Day).

There is no rule moving a holiday that falls on a Saturday, and the Labour Department's published lists keep Saturday holidays on the Saturday: its 2026 list shows Emancipation Day on 1 August and Boxing Day on 26 December, both Saturdays that year. In 2027 that means Labour Day on Saturday 1 May and Christmas Day on Saturday 25 December are not moved to a weekday.

The Sunday rule is applied in practice. The Labour Department's 2025 list includes an "Independence Day Holiday" on Monday 1 December, because 30 November 2025 was a Sunday. For 2027, the government calendar explicitly lists Emancipation Day as observed on Tuesday 3 August, following Kadooment Day on Monday 2 August.

The holidays one by one

January: New Year's Day and Errol Barrow Day

The year starts with a long weekend, since New Year's Day is a Friday. Errol Barrow Day follows on Thursday 21 January. January also brings Barbados Sailing Week, which Visit Barbados lists for 15 to 21 January 2027, so the holiday falls on its final day.

Easter: Good Friday and Easter Monday

Easter comes early in 2027, giving a four-day weekend from Friday 26 March to Monday 29 March. The Oistins Fish Festival takes place every Easter weekend in Oistins, Christ Church, according to Visit Barbados, so expect crowds and traffic on the south coast. If travelling over Easter, see our guide to Barbados in winter for booking advice.

National Heroes Day and Labour Day

National Heroes Day on Wednesday 28 April is a midweek holiday. Labour Day falls on Saturday 1 May in 2027 and is not moved.

Whit Monday

Whit Monday on 17 May creates a long weekend.

August: Kadooment Day and Emancipation Day

The first week of August includes consecutive public holidays. Crop Over, which the National Cultural Foundation describes as a festival of about three months, traditionally ends with the Grand Kadooment parade. Kadooment Day is Monday 2 August 2027; check the organiser for the 2027 parade programme. Emancipation Day falls on Sunday 1 August, so its public holiday moves to Tuesday 3 August. That gives a four-day break from Saturday 31 July to Tuesday 3 August. Plan around road closures on parade day and book accommodation early; our Crop Over guide has the details.

Independence Day

Independence Day falls on Tuesday 30 November 2027. Government offices and banks close, so check the official programme before planning visits. If you are in Bridgetown that week, the Parliament Buildings and Historic Bridgetown and its Garrison are worth a walk, but check opening hours on the day itself.

Christmas and Boxing Day

Christmas Day is a Saturday in 2027 and is not moved. Boxing Day falls on Sunday 26 December, so Monday 27 December is the public holiday. The result is a three-day weekend from Saturday 25 to Monday 27 December.

What closes on a public holiday

Section 4 of the Public Holidays Act says that, subject to exemptions, no place of business, government department or school may open on a public holiday. The Act defines a place of business widely, including banks, offices, shops, stores and warehouses. In practice, expect banks, government offices, schools and most shops to be closed. Get cash and do any bank errands before a long weekend; our currency and money guide explains your options.

The Second Schedule exempts a long list of businesses. In the 1998 consolidated text of the Act these include:

  • Hotels, clubs, boarding houses, restaurants and refreshment bars.
  • Hospitals, nursing homes and doctors' surgeries, and shops selling medicines while serving a customer.
  • Public transport companies, taxis and vehicle-hire garages.
  • Petrol stations, for fuel and urgent repairs.
  • Services at the harbour and the airport.
  • Licensed premises, for the sale of drinks and tobacco.
  • Shops selling fresh fish, fruit and vegetables, milk and ice, and newspapers.
  • Shops selling handicrafts of Common Market origin or products of cottage industries.
  • Cinemas and theatres.
  • The Barbados Turf Club and registered racing businesses.

Section 7 also lets a shop open on a holiday if the law on shop opening allows it. These exemptions permit hotels, restaurants, bars and taxis to operate, but do not guarantee normal service. Museums, attractions and tour operators set their own holiday hours. If a visit to the Barbados Museum, Harrison's Cave or St Nicholas Abbey falls on a holiday, check with the venue first. Bus services may run to a different timetable on holidays; see the transportation page and our guide to getting around Barbados.

Planning a trip around the 2027 holidays

  • For festival energy, aim for late July and early August, when Crop Over builds to Kadooment Day.
  • For quiet beaches, avoid the Easter weekend and the first week of August if you prefer to avoid holiday gatherings. Popular town beaches such as Carlisle Bay, Accra Beach and Paynes Bay are best early in the day on a long weekend.
  • Holiday evenings are a good time for the Oistins Fish Fry and the restaurants of Holetown and St Lawrence Gap, which are exempt from the closing rule.
  • Keep the emergency contacts to hand: hospitals stay open on every holiday.

For the weather in each month, see our best time to visit Barbados guide, and browse the events calendar for what is on.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many public holidays does Barbados have in 2027?

The Public Holidays Act lists twelve holidays. In 2027 all twelve are observed, two of them on a substitute weekday: Emancipation Day moves to Tuesday 3 August and Boxing Day to Monday 27 December, because 1 August and 26 December fall on Sundays.

When is Kadooment Day 2027?

Monday 2 August 2027. The Act makes the first Monday in August a public holiday. Grand Kadooment traditionally ends Crop Over, but check the organiser for its 2027 programme.

When is Emancipation Day 2027 observed?

Emancipation Day is 1 August, which is a Sunday in 2027. Under the Act, when 1 August falls on a Sunday or Monday, the next Tuesday is a public holiday, so it is observed on Tuesday 3 August 2027.

What happens if a Barbados public holiday falls on a Sunday?

For 1 January, 21 January, 28 April, 1 May, 30 November and 26 December, the next Monday becomes a public holiday. For 1 August and 25 December, the next Tuesday does. Holidays that fall on a Saturday are not moved.

When are Good Friday and Easter Monday in 2027?

Good Friday is 26 March and Easter Monday is 29 March 2027, since Easter Sunday falls on 28 March.

Are shops and restaurants open on public holidays in Barbados?

The Act closes banks, government offices, schools and most places of business, but exempts hotels, restaurants, bars, clubs, taxis, public transport, petrol stations, hospitals and several other businesses. Attractions set their own hours, so check before you go.

Has the government published the official 2027 list?

Yes. As of November 2026, the Government of Barbados calendar lists the 2027 holidays and the substitute days for Emancipation Day and Boxing Day. Check it again before travelling, as extra holidays can be appointed by order.

guides.title: Best Beaches in Barbados: 20 Beaches by Coast and Purpose
guides.summary: Twenty Barbados beaches compared: where the water is calm, which beaches have lifeguards, where to snorkel with turtles, and which Atlantic beaches are for looking, not swimming.
guides.html:
Barbados has two seas and three moods. The west coast faces the Caribbean and is usually calm enough to float in. The south coast catches the trade winds, with reef-protected bays and lively breaks. The east and south east face the open Atlantic, where the scenery is the best on the island and the water is often too rough to swim in. Picking a beach is mostly a matter of picking a coast, and this guide sorts the 20 beaches we cover by coast first and then by what each one suits.

Two facts shape every beach day here. First, Visit Barbados, the island's tourism authority, states that all beaches in Barbados are open to the public and access to them is a right of every Barbadian. Second, conditions change with the season and the tide, and lifeguards are only at some beaches for part of the day. Read the safety section before you head to the Atlantic side.

Quick picks by what you want

  • Calmest swimming: Paynes Bay, Mullins Beach, Heywoods Beach and the cove side of Miami Beach.
  • Families with young children: Folkestone Beach, Batts Rock Beach, Accra Beach and, on the east coast, Bath Beach.
  • Snorkelling and turtles: Carlisle Bay, Paynes Bay, Folkestone and Dover Beach.
  • Surf, wind and scenery: Bathsheba (the Soup Bowl), Silver Sands, Crane Beach, Bottom Bay, Foul Bay and Cattlewash.

Carlisle Bay and the Bridgetown beaches

Bridgetown has Carlisle Bay to the south and other beaches north of the port in St Michael. The bay is a protected marine area, the Carlisle Bay Marine Park, managed by the Coastal Zone Management Unit, with six major wrecks listed by Visit Barbados. Visit Barbados names Carlisle Bay among the top places to see sea turtles, making it an option to consider if you are staying in town or on the south coast.

  • Carlisle Bay is the main stretch of sand, usually calm, with catamarans and snorkel boats coming and going. The Browne's Beach section has lifeguards on duty, according to the tourism authority.
  • Pebbles Beach is the southern end of the bay. Early in the morning, racehorses from the nearby Garrison are walked into the sea, and reef fish draw snorkellers once the horses have gone.
  • Brighton Beach lies north of the port, a long and roomy beach for a walk on the sand, with sunsets across open water.
  • Batts Rock Beach at Black Rock is narrow and sits below a cliff, but has showers, a play park, picnic benches and calm rock-free spots for casual swimmers. Visit Barbados notes it is popular with snorkellers.

Rules in the marine park are simple: do not take any sea life, do not fish, and do not touch or feed the turtles. The tourism authority advises snorkelling when few boats are around. If you would rather go with a guide, see swimming with turtles, snorkelling and catamaran cruises.

West coast: the calm Caribbean side

The St James and St Peter coast, running north from Bridgetown through Holetown to Speightstown, has the gentlest water on the island for most of the year. Visit Barbados describes the west coast as calm water and white sand. The one exception is the winter swell: the government's Coastal Zone Management Unit says high waves are generated from November to April and that the west coast feels the most severe effects. On a swell day, stay out unless a lifeguard advises that swimming is safe.

Calm swimming

  • Paynes Bay is a long, calm bay in St James and one of the beaches where the tourism authority says you can find turtles by swimming out from the shore.
  • Sandy Lane Beach has golden sand and clear water in front of the resort of the same name. It is public: Visit Barbados notes several access points. Chairs and restaurants are not readily available, so bring what you need.
  • Mullins Beach in St Peter has calm water that the tourism authority calls suitable for swimmers of all abilities, plus a restaurant and beach bar, jet skis and glass-bottom boats. It gets busy, so arrive early.
  • Gibbes Beach is another west coast option.
  • Heywoods Beach, just north of Speightstown, is for quiet sea baths and boat watching. Visit Barbados lists a lifeguard on duty but no beach facility.

Snorkelling and families

Folkestone Beach is the shore of the Folkestone Marine Park just north of Holetown: a protected inshore reef for snorkelling, a sunken barge, a small marine museum and picnic tables in the shade. As of November 2026 the tourism authority lists the park as open Monday to Friday from 9:00 to 17:00. It is the best all-round family beach on this coast, and the tourism authority's advice for the marine parks is to stay close to the shore. For diving further out, see scuba diving.

South coast: reefs, breeze and a bit of surf

The Christ Church coast between Hastings and Worthing and Oistins is a base to consider, and its beaches have restaurants and bars a few steps away. The water is often reef-protected but livelier than in the west. The National Conservation Commission currently lists patrols at Dover and Enterprise; check supervision on arrival.

  • Accra Beach (Rockley Beach) is wide, with room to spread out. At low tide, snorkellers can wade past the rocks to pools full of fish; at high tide the waves suit bodyboarding. There is a play park just behind the sand and buses stop close by.
  • Dover Beach sits beside St Lawrence Gap, a broad beach with hotels and bars nearby. Visit Barbados lists it among the top turtle-spotting places.
  • Miami Beach (Enterprise Beach) is two minutes from Oistins and has two faces: a sheltered cove on the western side for calm swimming and more swell and stronger currents on the eastern side, plus picnic tables, a beach facility and a lifeguard. Pair it with a visit to Oistins Fish Fry.
  • Silver Sands Beach, near the southern tip, is a quarter mile of pale sand with steady wind. Visit Barbados warns that undercurrents make it precarious for anyone who is not a strong swimmer. It is a wind beach first: see kitesurfing and windsurfing.

South east: cliffs, pink sand and big water

Around The Crane in St Philip, the coast turns to face the Atlantic. These beaches are some of the most photographed on the island, and the swimming advice changes with them.

  • Crane Beach is a cove of pink-tinged sand below the cliffs, with Atlantic waves that suit bodyboarding. The Crane Resort says its government lifeguard station is not staffed daily. Check that a lifeguard is present and follow their advice before swimming; never enter under a red flag.
  • Bottom Bay is a cove of sand and palms ringed by coral cliffs. The tourism authority says plainly that bathing is not recommended because the waves are very strong. Come for photos and a picnic.
  • Foul Bay is long, wide and usually empty. It is open to the Atlantic; current lifeguard cover could not be confirmed. Treat it as a beach for walking.

East coast: surf and scenery only (with one exception)

The east coast of St Joseph and St John, around Bathsheba and the Scotland District, is the island at its wildest: boulders in the surf, long empty sands and the trade winds blowing straight in. The UK government's travel advice says swimming is not recommended on many east coast beaches because the currents are particularly strong.

  • Bathsheba Beach is home to the Soup Bowl, the island's best-known surf break, with waves driven by the north east trade winds. Visit Barbados says it is not the best for the average swimmer. Watch the surfers from the sand, or read about surfing in Barbados if you ride waves yourself.
  • Cattlewash Beach runs beside the East Coast Road north of Bathsheba: a long walk on the sand with big waves. Check current supervision locally. Do not swim in the open sea here.
  • Bath Beach in St John is the exception. Offshore reefs calm the water, and the tourism authority says it has some of the calmest water on the east coast, with casuarina trees for shade and picnic space. Visit Barbados lists a lifeguard on duty, but families should check conditions and supervision before entering.

Consider combining a beach visit with sightseeing at Farley Hill National Park, Cherry Tree Hill or Andromeda Botanic Gardens; plan your route before setting out.

Swimming safety: what the official sources say

  • Atlantic side: on the east and south east coasts, assume the sea is unsafe unless you are at a lifeguarded beach and the flags say otherwise. Visit Barbados lists no lifeguard at Silver Sands. Lifeguard cover at Bottom Bay and Foul Bay could not be confirmed.
  • Calm coasts are not risk free: the UK travel advice warns that currents can be deceptively strong on some popular south and west coast beaches too, and that some beaches have no lifeguards or warning flags.
  • Flags: the National Conservation Commission says yellow means take care in moderate conditions and red means do not swim. No flag means the beach is not patrolled at that moment, not that swimming is safe.
  • Hours: lifeguard stations are not staffed around the clock. Swim during the day, near the station.
  • Winter swells from November to April hit the west coast hardest, so a normally calm bay can have breaking waves when swell reaches the shore.

Emergency numbers are on our emergency contacts page, and our safety guide covers the wider picture.

Public access and getting to the beach

Because every beach is public, reach it using designated public accesses. Public beach access does not give permission to cross private hotel or villa grounds. Use the public paths between properties, which are often narrow lanes off the main coast road. What is private is the hotel's sunbeds, bars and grounds, so expect to rent a chair or bring a towel.

The west and south coast beaches are on the main bus routes, and the BDS$3.50 flat fare, as of November 2026, gets you to most of them; see getting around Barbados. For the south east and east coast, a hire car or a taxi is more practical. Visitors no longer buy a driving permit: since 15 October 2025 the Barbados Revenue Authority's Car Rental Levy, collected by the rental company, has replaced it. As of November 2026 it is BBD 5 a day, capped at BBD 35 per rental and included in the rental fee.

Planning beach days

For seasonal weather and sea conditions, see the best time to visit Barbados and check the weather page. Choose your base by the kind of beach you want with where to stay in Barbados, and the 7-day family itinerary spreads the calm beaches across a week. All 20 beaches are on our beaches page.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which coast of Barbados has the calmest water?

The west coast. Visit Barbados describes it as calm water and white sand, and beaches such as Paynes Bay, Mullins and Heywoods are described as calm, but swimmers should check conditions and supervision. The exception is the winter swell from November to April, which the Coastal Zone Management Unit says hits the west coast hardest.

Are all beaches in Barbados public?

Yes. Visit Barbados states that all beaches in Barbados are open to the public and that access is a right of every Barbadian. Hotel sunbeds and facilities are private, but the sand is not, and public paths lead down between properties.

Can you swim on the east coast of Barbados?

Mostly not. The UK travel advice says swimming is not recommended on many east coast beaches because of strong currents, and Visit Barbados says bathing at Bottom Bay is not recommended. Bath Beach, where reefs calm the water and a lifeguard station is listed, is the main exception.

Where can I swim with turtles in Barbados?

Visit Barbados names Carlisle Bay, Holetown, Dover Beach and Drill Hall as top turtle-spotting places, and says turtles can also be found by swimming at Paynes Bay. Do not touch or feed them, and snorkel when few boats are around.

Which Barbados beaches have lifeguards?

The National Conservation Commission lists patrols at Miami (Enterprise), Dover and Browne's Beach. Visit Barbados also lists lifeguards at Accra (Rockley), Folkestone, Bathsheba, Bath and Heywoods, although Heywoods is absent from the National Conservation Commission supervised-beach list of February 2025, so do not rely on cover there. At Crane, the resort warns that the government station is not staffed daily. Stations are not staffed around the clock, so check the flags on arrival.

What is the best beach in Barbados for families?

Folkestone Beach suits families best on the west coast, with a protected snorkel reef, shade and picnic tables. On the south coast, Accra Beach has a play park and lifeguards, and the cove side of Miami Beach is calm.

guides.title: Best Time to Visit Barbados: Month-by-Month Guide
guides.summary: The driest, sunniest months in Barbados are February to April; the wet season and the Atlantic hurricane season run from June to November, and Crop Over fills July and early August.
guides.html:
The short version

Barbados is warm all year, so the question is less about heat and more about rain, crowds and what is on. The Barbados Meteorological Services (BMS) normals for 1991 to 2020 show average daily highs between about 29C and 31C (84F to 88F) in every month. What changes is the rain: March is the driest month on that record, with under 40mm, and October is the wettest, with close to 180mm.

For most visitors the choice comes down to three windows. December to May is the dry season. The winter months are a popular time for winter-sun travel. May and June are quieter, still mostly dry early on, and good value. June to November is the wet season and overlaps with the Atlantic hurricane season, but it also brings Crop Over, a major summer festival, and lower demand outside the festival weeks.

Barbados weather month by month

The table below uses the climate data sheet published by the Barbados Meteorological Services, whose office is in the Civil Aviation Department Building at Charnocks, Christ Church, near Grantley Adams International Airport. All figures are 1991 to 2020 averages. The sheet does not identify the observation station, so these figures should not be treated as measurements for every part of the island. Rain days are the average number of days with rain in the month.
