destinations.name: St Lucy and the northern tip
destinations.tagline: Rural northern parish of cliffs, sea caves and the Animal Flower Cave
destinations.summary: St Lucy is the rural north of Barbados: cliffs and jagged shoreline washed by the Atlantic, the Animal Flower Cave at the northern tip, and a slower pace of life.
destinations.html:
St Lucy is the northernmost parish of Barbados, a rural area of farms, small villages, rum shops and churches that sees far fewer visitors than the coasts to the south. The tourism board describes it as kissed on the north, east and west by the Atlantic, and the scenery is dramatic: rugged cliffs, a jagged shoreline and small white-sand coves tucked between the rocks. Life here moves noticeably slower than on the west and south coasts.

The main sight is the Animal Flower Cave at the northern tip of the island, a sea cave with openings to the ocean and rock pools of clear water, with a restaurant on the clifftop above. Elsewhere in the parish, the Harrison Point Lighthouse stands on the coast, and the north-west shore has a few small bays worth seeking out on a calm day. This is not a beach-holiday base: the open Atlantic swell makes most of the northern coast unsafe for swimming, and facilities are few.

What to do

  • Visit the Animal Flower Cave and look out from the cliffs at the northern tip.
  • Drive the quiet country roads, stopping at village rum shops and churches.
  • Combine the north with St Nicholas Abbey, Cherry Tree Hill and the Morgan Lewis Windmill on one loop.
  • Finish with a swim back on the calm west coast at Heywoods Beach near Speightstown.

St Lucy works best as a day trip by car or on a tour, usually from the west coast. Public buses reach the parish, but services are less frequent than on the coast road. Bring water and sun protection, wear shoes with grip around the cliffs and cave, and stay well back from the edge when the sea is up.

Speightstown is the nearest town and the obvious base, with Holetown further south. For the rest of the Atlantic side, continue down the east coast to Bathsheba. Our things to do in Barbados guide shows how to fit the north into a longer trip.

photo.alt: Rocky cliffs and Atlantic waves at North Point, St Lucy, Barbados

destinations.name: The Crane and St Philip
destinations.tagline: Pink-tinged sand, cliffs and secluded Atlantic bays on the south-east coast
destinations.summary: The Crane is the area around Crane Beach in St Philip: a cliff-backed bay on the south-east coast, close to Bottom Bay, Foul Bay and Sunbury Plantation House.
destinations.html:
The Crane is an area on the south-east coast of Barbados in St Philip, the largest of the island's eleven parishes. Its name comes from a small 18th-century port here, where cargo was raised and lowered by a crane on the cliff. In 1887 a hotel opened above the bay, and Crane Beach below it is a striking beach: sand with a pink tint, turquoise water and a cliff at its back.

This is where the two characters of Barbados meet. The south-east coast faces the Atlantic, but it is broken into bays and coves, some sheltered by reef and some open to the swell. Further along, Bottom Bay is a secluded cove reached by a steep stairway, beautiful for a picnic but, in the tourism board's words, not suitable for swimming because the seas are very aggressive. Foul Bay is a long, open sweep of sand for walks. Check conditions and lifeguard advice on any south-east beach before going in.

What to do

  • Spend a morning at Crane Beach and walk the cliffs above it.
  • Picnic at Bottom Bay and walk the long sands of Foul Bay.
  • Tour Sunbury Plantation House, its antiques and its collection of horse-drawn carriages.
  • Learn how rum is made at the Foursquare Rum Distillery (see rum tours).

St Philip is mostly rural, with villages, fields and a long coastline, so a car or a tour makes the most sense here. Resorts and villas offer places to stay along this stretch of coast. The airport is in neighbouring Christ Church, so The Crane is a realistic first or last night on a trip.

From here, the busy south coast of Oistins and St Lawrence Gap lies to the west, and the coast road north leads towards Bathsheba through St John, past Bath Beach. Our best beaches guide sets these Atlantic bays beside the calm west-coast ones.

beaches.name: Accra Beach (Rockley Beach)
beaches.tagline: Busy south coast beach with bodyboarding waves, vendors and food steps away
beaches.summary: A wide south coast beach in Rockley with room to spread out, reef pools at low tide, bodyboarding waves and shops and food across the road. Lifeguard supervised.
beaches.html:
Accra Beach is a public beach in Rockley in Christ Church, between Hastings and Worthing and the restaurants of St Lawrence Gap. It is a broad stretch of pale sand, partly framed by a low limestone cliff at one end, with enough space that it rarely feels cramped even on a busy weekend.

Limestone reef breaks the water offshore. At low tide snorkellers wade out past the rocks to sheltered pools with fish, and at higher tide the waves are good for bodyboarding, with the occasional surfer joining in. Visit Barbados lists a lifeguard on duty, so swim near the tower and follow the flags: a yellow flag means take care, a red flag means stay out of the water. The UK government's travel advice warns that currents can be deceptively strong even on popular south and west coast beaches.

Accra is the beach to pick if you want everything within a few steps. Vendors sell coconut water, snow cones and crafts on the sand, small huts on the edge of the beach sell beachwear and drinks, and beach chairs are rented under the trees. A boardwalk beside the beach passes cafes and bars, and there are shops and places to eat directly across the main road. A children's play park sits just behind the sand.

Before you go

  • Visit Barbados lists a lifeguard on duty; towers are not staffed around the clock.
  • Rented chairs, beach vendors, food and shops on and beside the beach.
  • Low tide is the time for reef pools; higher tide brings bodyboarding waves.
  • Easy to reach by the south coast buses and minibuses; parking nearby.

From Accra it is a short ride east to the livelier Dover Beach and the Friday night Oistins Fish Fry, or west towards Bridgetown and the swimming water of Carlisle Bay. For a wider plan, see our guide to the best beaches in Barbados.

beaches.name: Bath Beach
beaches.tagline: Reef-sheltered east coast beach in St John, more sheltered than much of this coast
beaches.summary: An east coast beach in St John where offshore reefs calm the water. Casuarina shade, picnic space, snorkelling and a lifeguard station; check sea conditions before swimming.
beaches.html:
Bath Beach is on the east coast in the parish of St John, south of Bathsheba. On a coast known for heavy surf it is the exception: coral reefs a short distance offshore break the Atlantic swell, so the water inside them is among the calmest on this side of Barbados. That makes Bath one of the few east coast beaches where a relaxed swim is realistic.

Tall casuarina trees line the back of the beach and give the shade that makes Bath a favourite picnic spot. Weekdays are usually quiet, while weekends and public holidays bring families and groups. The reefs, visible from the sand, are good for snorkelling in settled conditions, and hawksbill turtles nest on this stretch of coast, with hatching usually between July and October. Kayaking, stand-up paddling and walks to a freshwater spring that runs down to the sea are other ways to fill the day.

Visit Barbados lists a lifeguard on duty at Bath Beach. Calm by east coast standards does not mean calm everywhere: stay inside the reef, swim near the lifeguard tower and obey the flags. The UK government's travel advice notes that lifeguard stations are not staffed 24 hours a day.

Why go

  • Reef-sheltered water, among the calmest on the east coast.
  • Visit Barbados lists a lifeguard on duty.
  • Casuarina shade and space for picnics.
  • Snorkelling on the offshore reefs when the sea is settled.

Bath fits neatly into an east coast day with the surf and rock formations of Bathsheba Beach and the gardens at Andromeda Botanic Gardens. Hikers can look at our hiking page for walks in this part of the island.

beaches.name: Bathsheba Beach (the Soup Bowl)
beaches.tagline: Barbados's famous surf break, giant boulders and Atlantic views; not for swimming
beaches.summary: Home of the Soup Bowl surf break: golden sand, huge boulders and crashing Atlantic waves. Come to watch surfers and the sunrise; open-sea swimming is unsafe.
beaches.html:
Bathsheba Beach lines the east coast at the fishing village of Bathsheba in St Joseph, below the green hills of the Scotland District. Golden sand, coconut palms and great boulders standing in the surf make it one of the most dramatic places in Barbados, and the drive down to it is half the experience.

It is best known for the Soup Bowl, the surf break that has made Bathsheba the centre of surfing in Barbados. The name dates from the 1960s: the curling face of the wave is the bowl, and the whitewater after it breaks is the soup. Waves arrive for most of the year, driven by the north-east trade winds, and the biggest swells come in the winter months. Beginners can learn here with an instructor in the smaller, calmer conditions of early morning at low tide; when the swell is big, the Bowl is for experienced surfers.

This is not a swimming beach. Visit Barbados says Bathsheba is not the best for the average swimmer, and the UK government's travel advice states that swimming is not recommended on many east-coast beaches where currents are particularly strong. Visit Barbados lists lifeguards on duty at Bathsheba, but towers are not staffed at all hours. Paddle only in the shallow rock pools when the sea is calm, obey the flags and stay out of the open water.

Safety and practical tips

  • Open-sea swimming is unsafe: strong currents and heavy surf.
  • Visit Barbados lists a lifeguard on duty; obey the flags.
  • Surfboard rental and lessons are available locally.
  • A few rum shops and restaurants in the village across the road.

Bathsheba is the base for an east coast day: walk north to Cattlewash Beach, visit Andromeda Botanic Gardens or the Flower Forest, and finish at the calmer water of Bath Beach to the south.

beaches.name: Batts Rock Beach
beaches.tagline: Snorkellers' cove below a quiet cliff at Black Rock
beaches.summary: A narrow beach below a cliff at Black Rock, St Michael, with flat rocks full of small fish, calm swimming spots, showers, a play park and picnic benches.
beaches.html:
Batts Rock Beach sits at the bottom of a winding road at Black Rock in St Michael, on the west coast north of Bridgetown. Visit Barbados describes it as a narrow strip of sand beside a quiet cliff, without the wide white beaches found further up the coast. That is part of its appeal: it is a beach that many visitors drive past.

The flat rocks close to shore are the main reason to come. They mean swimmers sometimes need to go a little further out before the water is clear of rock, but they also hold small fish, which makes Batts Rock a favourite with snorkellers. There are several rock-free patches where the water is clear and calm enough for an easy swim. For a small beach it is well set up, with parking, showers and changing facilities, picnic benches, a children's play park and a beach bar and restaurant. Stay for the evening: the uphill path back from the beach is a good place to watch the sun set as catamarans head back to port.

Know before you go

  • Flat rocks near the shore: wear water shoes and pick a rock-free spot to enter.
  • Good snorkelling over the rocks for small reef fish.
  • Parking, showers, changing rooms, picnic benches and a play park.
  • Winter swells from November to April can affect the west coast.

Batts Rock is a short hop from Brighton Beach to the south and the turtle waters of Paynes Bay to the north. See our snorkelling guide for other easy entry points, and the catamaran cruises page for trips that pass this stretch of coast.

beaches.name: Bottom Bay
beaches.tagline: Palm-lined cove under coral cliffs; a picnic spot, not a swimming beach
beaches.summary: A cove of sand and palms ringed by coral cliffs on the south-east coast. Spectacular for photos and picnics, but strong waves make bathing here unsafe for most.
beaches.html:
Bottom Bay is a small, half-enclosed bay on the south-east coast in St Philip, just north of Crane Beach in the area of The Crane and St Philip. High coral cliffs wrap around the sand, tall coconut palms stand along the back of the beach, and the view from the clifftop down into the bay is a reason to come even if you never touch the water.

Come for the scenery and a picnic, not for a swim. Visit Barbados states plainly that bathing here is not recommended because the waves are very strong, and current lifeguard coverage could not be confirmed. The UK government's travel advice warns that swimming is not recommended on many east-coast beaches, where currents are particularly strong. Stay on the sand and keep children away from the surf.

The beach is reached on foot from the clifftop, so wear shoes with grip. Bring water, food and shade rather than relying on facilities, and take your rubbish home. People who live on the cliffs report seeing turtles and whales offshore, so it is worth scanning the water while you are here.

Know before you go

  • Bathing not recommended: strong waves; supervision unconfirmed.
  • Bring everything you need rather than relying on facilities.
  • Access on foot from the clifftop; expect uneven ground.
  • Best for photographs, picnics and a quiet walk on the sand.

Pair Bottom Bay with Crane Beach to check conditions, and with Foul Bay for a longer walk on the sand. Our Barbados safety guide covers sea conditions around the island.

beaches.name: Brighton Beach
beaches.tagline: Long, local stretch of west coast sand just north of the port
beaches.summary: A long stretch of sand in Brighton, St Michael, just north of Bridgetown's port. Calm west coast water and room to spread out without the resort crowds.
beaches.html:
Brighton Beach runs along the west coast of St Michael, a short drive north of Bridgetown and its deep-water cruise port. A tourism brochure hosted by Visit Barbados describes Brighton as a long, usually quiet strand of soft white sand off the Spring Garden Highway. Further north is Batts Rock Beach.

The sand is long and open, and the west coast water is generally calm, which makes it a practical choice for a swim close to town or a quiet hour after a morning in the city. Its west coast setting makes late afternoon a good time to enjoy the sunset.

Practical notes

  • Long, open stretch of sand on the west coast of St Michael.
  • Usually calm water; winter swells from November to April can bring bigger waves.
  • Public facilities at Brighton itself are not confirmed, so bring water and shade.
  • Face west for the sunset in the late afternoon.

Brighton pairs well with a visit to Historic Bridgetown and its Garrison, or with snorkelling further up the coast at Batts Rock Beach. For turtles and wrecks, head south to Carlisle Bay.

beaches.name: Carlisle Bay
beaches.tagline: Bridgetown's sheltered bay of shipwrecks, reef fish and green turtles
beaches.summary: The calm bay beside Bridgetown, with a protected marine area holding six major wrecks, regular turtle sightings and lifeguards at Browne's Beach.
beaches.html:
Carlisle Bay curves along the southwest coast of Barbados between the Careenage in Bridgetown and Needham's Point, in the parish of St Michael. The bay takes its name from James Hay, 1st Earl of Carlisle, the island's second Lord Proprietor, and the Needham's Point Lighthouse stands at its southern end. The bay has several named beach stretches: Browne's Beach runs along Bay Street close to the city, and Pebbles Beach sits further south towards the point.

What makes the bay special lies under the surface. To protect its marine life and six major wrecks, Carlisle Bay is a designated protected area managed by the Coastal Zone Management Unit, which has kept adding to the dive and snorkel site by sinking further wrecks. One named addition is the MV Trident, a former coast guard flagship sunk on 28 April 2016; dive operators treat it as a separate, deeper dive close to the bay rather than part of the shallow six-wreck circuit. Anchors, cannonballs and other relics from older ships lie on the seabed, and the bay is one of the places Visit Barbados lists as a top spot to see sea turtles.

Before you swim

  • Lifeguards are on duty at Browne's Beach, which has showers and changing facilities near the car park.
  • Snorkel when few boats are around, and do not touch or feed the turtles.
  • Take nothing from the reef or the wrecks: the Coastal Zone Management Unit advises against collecting coral or marine life.
  • Winter swells from November to April can stir up the water on the west and south coasts.

Read more about the protected area on our Carlisle Bay Marine Park page, then plan your time in the water with our guides to swimming with turtles, snorkelling and scuba diving. The bay is near Historic Bridgetown and its Garrison. Browse catamaran cruises if you would rather reach the bay by boat.

beaches.name: Cattlewash Beach
beaches.tagline: Long, empty east coast beach beside the coast road north of Bathsheba
beaches.summary: A long stretch of sand beside the East Coast Road north of Bathsheba, with big Atlantic waves and room to walk. Strong currents and unconfirmed supervision: plan a walk.
beaches.html:
Cattlewash is the long beach that runs beside the East Coast Road just north of Bathsheba, in the Scotland District of the east coast. The sand stretches a long way, the Atlantic rolls in white along its whole length, and on most days you will share it with very few people. It is a beach for walking, sitting and watching the sea rather than for swimming.

The water here is dangerous for most visitors. The UK government's travel advice states that swimming is not recommended on many east-coast beaches where currents are particularly strong, and current lifeguard coverage at Cattlewash could not be confirmed. Current lifeguard coverage could not be confirmed. Do not rely on supervision, and follow local sea warnings. Keep to the sand, keep children out of the surf, and stay out of the water.

Because the road runs right alongside, Cattlewash is easy to reach by car or on an east coast drive, and it is a good place to stop for photographs of the coastline curving north. Do not rely on facilities being available on the sand; bring water and shade and plan food and drink stops in advance.

Before you stop

  • Swimming not advised: strong east coast currents and heavy surf.
  • Current lifeguard coverage unconfirmed.
  • Bring supplies; confirm facilities locally.
  • Roadside access along the East Coast Road.

Pair a walk at Cattlewash with the surf at Bathsheba Beach and the gardens of Andromeda Botanic Gardens. For a more sheltered option on this coast, check conditions at Bath Beach. Our Barbados safety guide has more on sea conditions.

beaches.name: Crane Beach
beaches.tagline: Pink-tinged sand below the cliffs of St Philip on the south-east coast
beaches.summary: A cliff-backed cove of pink-tinged sand on the south-east coast, with Atlantic waves and a government lifeguard station that is not manned daily.
beaches.html:
Crane Beach lies at the foot of the cliffs in St Philip on the south-east coast, in the area our guide covers as The Crane and St Philip. The sand has a pink tinge, the water runs from pale turquoise to deep blue, and the cove is framed by the cliff on which The Crane resort has stood since 1887. It makes a striking setting for photographs and a long afternoon on the sand.

The sea here faces the Atlantic side of the island. Waves roll in steadily and are popular with bodyboarders, and conditions change with the swell: some days are fine for a careful swim, others are rough. The Crane resort says a government lifeguard is provided, but the station is not manned daily. Stay close to the lifeguard tower, never swim when the red flag is flying, and treat a yellow flag as a real warning. The UK government's travel advice is blunt about the east side of Barbados: currents can be particularly strong, and you should follow local warnings.

The NCC lists a public pedestrian access to The Crane. The resort also describes a staircase and glass-front beach elevator; as of November 2026, its elevator and stairs are locked at sundown. Check with the resort about access for non-guests. Its Beach Hut supplies umbrellas and loungers to hotel guests, and The Grove serves drinks and light meals. Bring water and sun protection.

Before you go

  • Government lifeguard station, but not manned daily; obey the flags.
  • Atlantic swell: good for bodyboarding, sometimes too rough to swim.
  • Public pedestrian access is listed by the NCC; resort stairs and elevator lock at sundown as of November 2026.
  • Resort beach services are available; check non-guest access before relying on them.

Crane combines well with the cliff-top views of Bottom Bay and the long sands of Foul Bay, both close by in St Philip. Sunbury Plantation House is a short drive inland, and the airport is close enough to make this a good first or last stop.

beaches.name: Dover Beach
beaches.tagline: Wide sandy beach at the St Lawrence Gap end of the south coast
beaches.summary: A broad sandy beach beside St Lawrence Gap with hotels, bars and restaurants a short walk away. Lifeguard supervised and handy for a beach day near your base.
beaches.html:
Dover Beach runs along the eastern end of St Lawrence Gap in Christ Church, the strip of hotels, bars and restaurants that keeps the south coast busy after dark. By day the beach is the quieter half of that picture: a wide band of sand in front of small hotels and apartments, with sea views straight out across the south coast.

Because it sits on the doorstep of so much accommodation, it can work as a practical beach for anyone staying in the Gap or Dover. The National Conservation Commission lists Dover among its lifeguard-supervised beaches, so the usual rules apply: swim in front of the tower, and treat a yellow flag as a warning and a red flag as a no-swimming signal. Wind and waves on the south coast change with the weather, and the UK government's travel advice notes that currents can be deceptively strong on popular south coast beaches.

Food and drink are never far away. The restaurants and bars of the Gap start a few steps inland, and the evening scene there is the main reason many people base themselves on this stretch. Bring water and sun protection for the beach itself, and plan a late afternoon swim before heading up to the Gap for dinner.

Good to know

  • Listed by the NCC as a lifeguard-supervised beach.
  • Hotels, bars and restaurants of St Lawrence Gap a short walk away.
  • South coast buses and minibuses run along the main road nearby.
  • Check the flag at the lifeguard tower before you swim.

Dover sits between Accra Beach to the west and Oistins to the east, where the Oistins Fish Fry is the classic Friday night out. For a calmer swim, the sheltered side of Miami Beach is a short ride along the coast.

beaches.name: Folkestone Beach
beaches.tagline: Holetown's marine park beach with an inshore snorkelling reef
beaches.summary: The beach of Folkestone Marine Park, just north of Holetown: a protected inshore reef for snorkelling, a sunken barge, a marine museum and shaded picnic tables.
beaches.html:
Folkestone Beach is the shoreline of the Folkestone Marine Park at Holetown, St James. The NCC describes the reserve as extending from just north of the Coral Reef Club Hotel to the southern edge of the Sandy Lane Hotel property, and Visit Barbados describes it as a protected area for snorkelling in the calm waters of the west coast. The NCC identifies Folkestone as Barbados' only legislated Marine Protected Area; Visit Barbados also describes Carlisle Bay as a marine park.

The reason to come is the reef close to shore. Fish move through the coral and gather around a sunken barge, all within reach of a snorkeller who stays near the beach, which is exactly what Visit Barbados advises for safety. Further out, divers visit the SS Stavronikita, a freighter deliberately sunk as an artificial reef, whose deck lies between about 75 and 100 feet. On land, the park has equipment rental, a marine life information centre and museum, and picnic tables in the shade. As of November 2026 Visit Barbados lists the park as open Monday to Friday from 9:00 to 17:00.

Snorkelling at Folkestone

  • Stay close to shore and over the inshore reef.
  • Do not remove coral or sea life; fishing within the reserve is prohibited.
  • Equipment rental and a marine museum are on site.
  • Winter swells from November to April hit the west coast hardest, so check the sea first.

Find out more about the protected area on our Folkestone Marine Park page, or plan a dive with our scuba diving guide. Holetown's restaurants and the Holetown Festival grounds are south, and the reserve extends south to the Sandy Lane Hotel property by Sandy Lane Beach.

beaches.name: Foul Bay
beaches.tagline: Long, open sweep of sand on the south-east coast, quiet on most days
beaches.summary: A long, wide south-east coast beach in St Philip with plenty of space and few people. Open to Atlantic waves, with supervision unconfirmed, so plan for walks and picnics.
beaches.html:
Foul Bay is a long, open sweep of sand on the south-east coast in St Philip, a short drive from Crane Beach and from the airport, in the area our guide calls The Crane and St Philip. The beach is long and open, with room to walk a long way without meeting many people.

The bay faces the open sea to the south-east. Follow local sea warnings. Current lifeguard coverage could not be confirmed, so do not rely on supervision. The UK government's travel advice warns that currents on the east-side beaches can be particularly strong. Treat Foul Bay as a place for walking and picnics, and check local sea warnings before approaching the surf.

Do not rely on facilities or rentals being available on the sand. Bring water, food and shade, and plan to spend an unhurried hour or two. Take your rubbish with you.

Plan your visit

  • Current lifeguard coverage unconfirmed; do not rely on supervision.
  • Bring water, food and shade rather than relying on facilities.
  • Wide sand and few people, good for long walks.
  • Close to Crane Beach and the airport for a first or last day.

Combine Foul Bay with Crane Beach, where there is a lifeguard tower, and the cliff views of Bottom Bay. If you have a few hours before a flight from Grantley Adams International Airport, check your route and allow enough time to return to the airport.

beaches.name: Gibbes Beach
beaches.tagline: Quiet St Peter bay just south of Mullins
beaches.summary: A quieter stretch of west coast sand in St Peter, just south of Mullins and Speightstown. Calm water most of the year and few crowds.
beaches.html:
Gibbes Beach lines Gibbes Bay in St Peter, immediately south of Mullins Beach and a short drive from Speightstown. Visit Barbados describes Gibbes as peaceful, with clear water for snorkelling.

Like the rest of the west coast, the water here is usually calm and clear, good for a swim or a lazy float, and it gets the evening sun. We could not confirm any facilities on the sand, so bring your own supplies or walk over to Mullins for food and drink. It suits anyone who wants space and silence rather than music and sunbeds. Swells in the winter months, from November to April, can reach this part of the coast, so check the sea before you go in.

Good to know

  • Quiet, sandy bay next to Mullins.
  • Usually calm water; winter swells can bring waves.
  • Bring water and shade, or walk to Mullins for food and drink.
  • Good spot to watch the sunset over the Caribbean Sea.

Combine Gibbes with lunch at Mullins Beach, an afternoon in Speightstown, or a quieter swim further north at Heywoods Beach.

beaches.name: Heywoods Beach
beaches.tagline: Quiet sea baths north of Speightstown
beaches.summary: A quiet beach just north of Speightstown, good for calm sea baths and watching boats. Lifeguard cover is not confirmed; bring water, food and shade.
beaches.html:
Heywoods Beach runs along the coast of St Peter just north of Speightstown, about 26 kilometres from Grantley Adams International Airport. Visit Barbados sums it up as the perfect place for quiet sea baths and boat watching, and that is the mood: a shore for floating in calm water and watching the boats go by.

Visit Barbados lists no beach facility. Its lifeguard claim is not corroborated by the latest complete NCC named list we could read, published in February 2025, so do not rely on supervision here. Bring water, food and shade, and use the shops and cafes in Speightstown before you arrive. The water is usually calm, as along the rest of the west coast, but swells in the winter months between November and April can make it rougher, so check conditions before entering the water.

What to expect

  • Lifeguard cover is not confirmed; do not rely on supervision.
  • No beach facility: bring your own water, food and shade.
  • Calm water for a sea bath in normal conditions.
  • Bring supplies before leaving Speightstown.

Heywoods is a good last stop on a drive up the west coast after Mullins Beach and Gibbes Beach. Continue north to explore St Lucy and the northern tip, or head back into Speightstown for dinner.

beaches.name: Miami Beach (Enterprise Beach)
beaches.tagline: Two-sided beach near Oistins: a sheltered western side and a wavier eastern side
beaches.summary: Enterprise, known locally as Miami Beach, near Oistins: a sheltered cove for calm swimming on one side, bigger waves on the other, picnic tables and a lifeguard.
beaches.html:
Miami Beach is the local name for Enterprise Beach, near Oistins in Christ Church. A rocky point splits it into two quite different beaches. On the western side, a sheltered cove has calmer water, while the eastern side catches more swell and has stronger currents.

It is very much a beach used by Barbadians as well as visitors, with early morning swimmers and weekend family groups gathering at the picnic tables along the back of the sand. There is a beach facility on site. The National Conservation Commission lists Enterprise among its lifeguard-supervised beaches, and the tower covers the swimming area. Coverage can be interrupted, including by seaweed. Swim on the sheltered side if you want calm water, and on the wavier side keep within sight of the tower and obey the flags.

Miami Beach pairs naturally with an evening in Oistins. Spend the afternoon on the sand, then head into town for the Oistins Fish Fry, where grilled fish and the Friday night crowd make it one of the island's best-known evenings out.

What to expect

  • Sheltered western side; more swell and stronger currents on the eastern side.
  • Picnic tables and a beach facility.
  • Listed by the NCC as a lifeguard-supervised beach.
  • Two minutes from Oistins and its Friday night fish fry.

Further east, the surf and wind of Silver Sands Beach draw windsurfers and kitesurfers, while Dover Beach and St Lawrence Gap lie a short ride west. If you are planning watersports, see our pages on surfing and kitesurfing and windsurfing.

beaches.name: Mullins Beach
beaches.tagline: Lively St Peter beach with calm water and a beach bar
beaches.summary: A popular St Peter beach near Speightstown with white sand, calm turquoise water, palms, a beach restaurant and bar, jet skis and glass-bottom boats.
beaches.html:
Mullins Beach sits on the St Peter coast just south of Speightstown, about 24 kilometres from Grantley Adams International Airport. Visit Barbados describes clear turquoise water, a sweeping length of white sand and coconut palms framing the bay, and calls the waves calm enough for swimmers of all abilities.

It is one of the livelier west coast beaches. A restaurant and beach bar sits on the sand, jet skis run off the shore, and glass-bottom boats take visitors out for a look at the seabed without getting wet. That popularity means the beach can get crowded, so arrive early if you want a good spot. Families like the gentle entry and the easy access, while the bar keeps things social through the afternoon. Even here, the winter swells that reach the west coast between November and April can change conditions, so check the water before swimming.

Planning a Mullins day

  • Calm, clear water suited to swimmers of all levels in normal conditions.
  • A beach restaurant and bar on the sand; jet skis and glass-bottom boats.
  • Gets busy: arrive in the morning for space.
  • West-facing for sunsets over the Caribbean Sea.

Mullins is close to the quieter Gibbes Beach next door and to Heywoods Beach north of Speightstown. Spend the rest of the day in Speightstown's old streets, or take to the water with our snorkelling and catamaran cruise guides.

beaches.name: Paynes Bay
beaches.tagline: St James bay where boat trips stop to swim with green turtles
beaches.summary: A calm St James bay between Batts Rock and Sandy Lane, named by Visit Barbados as a place to find sea turtles by swimming. Clear, usually calm water.
beaches.html:
Paynes Bay lies on the St James coast south of Holetown, between the Fitts Village shore and Sandy Lane Beach. The NCC lists pedestrian beach access at Paynes Bay Fish Market and Blue Monkey. The water is typically calm, clear and good for swimming, as on most of the sheltered west coast.

Turtles are the main draw. Visit Barbados names Paynes Bay as one of the places where you can find sea turtles while swimming, noting that they are further out here than at Alleyne's Beach in Holetown. The west coast is home to juvenile green turtles. Hawksbill turtles also nest on the west and south coasts of Barbados, so marked nests may appear on the sand. As everywhere, keep your distance, do not touch or feed the turtles, and swim out only within your ability.

Swimming at Paynes Bay

  • Calm, clear water most of the year; winter swells from November to April can bring waves.
  • Turtles are found by swimming out from the shore or on a boat trip.
  • Keep clear of moored boats and watersports lanes when swimming out.
  • Give nesting turtles space and report any problem to the Sea Turtle Hotline.

For the best chance of an up-close sighting, read our guide to swimming with turtles and compare catamaran cruises that stop in the bay. Holetown's restaurants and the Folkestone Marine Park are north of the bay.

beaches.name: Pebbles Beach
beaches.tagline: White-sand beach near the Garrison where racehorses swim at dawn
beaches.summary: A white-sand beach on the south side of Carlisle Bay, five minutes by car from Bridgetown. Racehorses take to the water early, and reef fish draw snorkellers.
beaches.html:
Pebbles Beach lines the southern part of Carlisle Bay in St Michael, about 2.7 kilometres from central Bridgetown and roughly 12.7 kilometres from Grantley Adams International Airport. Despite the name, it is a beach of white sand, with the Hilton hotel on Needham's Point as its backdrop and the rest of Carlisle Bay curving away towards the city.

The day starts early here. Visit Barbados describes the beach as the unofficial morning hangout of racehorses and their handlers, who lead the horses into the sea at sunrise, a sight that links the beach to the racing tradition of the nearby Garrison Savannah. Later in the morning the water belongs to swimmers, paddleboarders and boogie boarders. Reef fish live in the shallows, so bring a mask or rent snorkelling gear.

Good to know

  • White sand and clear, usually calm water on the sheltered southwest coast.
  • Come at sunrise to watch the horses being bathed.
  • Reef fish in the shallows make it a good first snorkel.
  • Winter swells from November to April can make the water rougher.

Pebbles is an easy add-on to a morning in Historic Bridgetown and its Garrison. For turtles and wrecks, swim or take a boat out into the Carlisle Bay Marine Park, and if you want more of the south coast, the beaches around Hastings, Rockley and Worthing are a short drive east.

beaches.name: Sandy Lane Beach
beaches.tagline: Famous golden-sand bay on the St James coast, open to all
beaches.summary: A golden-sand bay on the St James coast with clear, gentle water and nearby reefs. Public access paths lead to the sand; bring a picnic, as services are few.
beaches.html:
Sandy Lane Beach is the bay in front of the Sandy Lane resort in St James, just south of Holetown and about 19 kilometres from Grantley Adams International Airport. Visit Barbados describes clean golden sand meeting clear water, and a calm, peaceful bay where small waves lap the shore. The beach is well known for its famous neighbours, and celebrity spotting is part of its reputation.

The famous name does not make the beach private. Visit Barbados states that all beaches in Barbados are open to the public and that access to them is considered a right of every Barbadian, and there are several public access points to the sand. What the public part of the beach lacks is services: beach chairs and restaurants are not readily available to non-guests, so bring a picnic, water and something for shade. The water is good for swimming, although there can be some undertow, and the nearby coral reefs make for rewarding snorkelling. During the nesting season, a hawksbill turtle or two may come ashore.

Visiting Sandy Lane Beach

  • Reach the sand by the public access paths; a shower is available at the beach access.
  • Bring food, water and shade: beach chairs and restaurants are not readily available.
  • Good swimming, but watch for undertow, especially when winter swells arrive.
  • Snorkel along the reefs; leave nesting turtles and marked nests undisturbed.

Sandy Lane sits at the southern edge of the Folkestone Marine Park area, with Paynes Bay and its turtles just to the south and Folkestone Beach a short drive north. The name also belongs to a major race on the island's calendar, the Sandy Lane Gold Cup.

beaches.name: Silver Sands Beach
beaches.tagline: Windy south point beach for windsurfing and kitesurfing, not easy swimming
beaches.summary: Near the South Point Lighthouse: pale sand, steady wind and surf that draw windsurfers and kitesurfers. Undercurrents make it a poor choice for weaker swimmers.
beaches.html:
Silver Sands sits near the southernmost tip of Barbados in Christ Church, a short distance from the South Point Lighthouse and roughly a fifteen-minute drive from Oistins. The beach is a stretch of very pale sand of about a quarter of a mile, backed by low dunes, and the turn-off can be a little hard to find, so allow time and ask if you get lost.

What defines Silver Sands is the wind. Steady breezes and surf make it one of the island's main spots for windsurfing and kitesurfing, and the winter months, especially December and January, draw windsurfers and kitesurfers for the winter waves. Watching from the sand is half the entertainment.

For swimmers it is a different story. Visit Barbados describes the undercurrents here as precarious for anyone who is not a strong swimmer, and Visit Barbados lists no lifeguard on duty. It is not recommended for casual swimming. Stay on the sand to watch the riders.

Practical details

  • Visit Barbados lists no lifeguard on duty.
  • Changing facilities, equipment rentals and small food shops within walking distance.
  • No beach chair vendors, so bring towels and shade.
  • A play park and some accommodation sit close to the beach.

For calmer water nearby, head west to the sheltered cove at Miami Beach, then on to Oistins for the Oistins Fish Fry. The cliffs and pink-tinged sand of Crane Beach are a drive east along the south-east coast.
